A1.name: Fine-grained reactivity
A1.yes_means: A state change updates only the nodes that depend on it (signals or property bindings); no tree rebuild or diff.
A1.why: Update cost scales with what changed, not with the size of the UI.

A2.name: Compiled UI wiring
A2.yes_means: The UI description is compiled to direct update code; no runtime template interpreter or virtual tree. N/A for immediate-mode APIs.
A2.why: Removes runtime machinery from the binary and from the hot path.

A3.name: Batched updates
A3.yes_means: Many state changes in one tick produce one update, one layout and one paint.
A3.why: Prevents redundant work and visible intermediate states.

B1.name: Minimal retained state
B1.yes_means: No widget-object tree that mirrors app state: immediate mode, or a small ID-keyed cache.
B1.why: Less memory, and no bugs from keeping two copies of state in sync.

B2.name: Flat data layout
B2.yes_means: Nodes live in contiguous arrays or arenas and are referenced by index; no heap object and virtual call per widget.
B2.why: Fewer allocations and cache misses; cheap to traverse.

B3.name: Allocation-free steady state
B3.yes_means: A frame in which nothing structural changes performs no heap allocation.
B3.why: Predictable frame times; no allocator churn.

B4.name: No GC or managed runtime
B4.yes_means: No garbage collector, VM or script engine in the process.
B4.why: No pauses, a smaller footprint and a faster start.

C1.name: Bounded-pass layout
C1.yes_means: Layout finishes in one pass or a fixed number of passes; no general constraint solver or repeated measure loops.
C1.why: Layout cost is linear and predictable.

C2.name: Incremental layout
C2.yes_means: Only dirty subtrees are laid out again.
C2.why: Small changes stay cheap in large UIs.

D1.name: Small render and text stack
D1.yes_means: No bundled browser engine or large 2D library: a small renderer plus a modest or OS-provided text stack.
D1.why: Usually the largest share of binary size and memory.

D2.name: Batched GPU renderer
D2.yes_means: Few pipelines, instanced or batched draws, glyph atlas.
D2.why: Low CPU and GPU cost per frame.

D3.name: Software renderer
D3.why: Avoids graphics-driver memory overhead; needed on small devices and in VMs.

D4.name: Damage tracking
D4.why: Cuts fill cost and power for small changes.

D5.name: Zero work when idle
D5.yes_means: Event-driven: no layout, paint or wake-ups while nothing changes.

E1.name: Built-in list virtualization
E1.yes_means: Only visible rows are built and laid out.
E1.why: Cost scales with the screen, not with the data.

E2.name: Small binary, fast startup
E2.yes_means: A minimal app is a few MB or less and starts without booting a runtime.
E2.why: Download size and time to first frame.

E3.name: Runs on microcontrollers
E3.yes_means: Documented to run in well under 1 MB of RAM.
E3.why: Evidence that the core really is small.

F1.name: Async and background work
F1.yes_means: A built-in way to run work off the UI thread and deliver results back.
F1.why: The UI thread never blocks on I/O or computation.

F2.name: Frame-clock animation
F2.yes_means: Built-in animations driven by the frame clock, redrawing only what animates.
F2.why: Smooth motion without continuous full redraw.

F3.name: Decoupled render thread
F3.yes_means: Rendering can proceed on a thread separate from UI logic.
F3.why: Slow app code does not stall scrolling or animation.

G1.name: First-class custom widgets
G1.yes_means: User widgets implement their own layout, paint and input through the same API the built-ins use.
G1.why: No ceiling on what can be built.

G2.name: Unstyled, fully themable
G2.yes_means: No fixed look: every visual of every widget can be replaced.

G3.name: Custom shaders on elements
G3.yes_means: User shaders or materials can be attached to UI elements.
G3.why: Visual effects without leaving the UI system.

G4.name: Raw GPU access inline
G4.yes_means: User code gets the device and queue and issues its own draw calls inside the framework's render pass, at the right z-order.
G4.why: Full control: 3D views, custom pipelines, zero-copy integration.

G5.name: Texture interop
G5.yes_means: Externally rendered GPU textures can be shown as UI images, or the UI can be rendered into a user-supplied texture.
G5.why: Embedding engines, video and offscreen content.

G6.name: Pluggable renderer
G6.yes_means: The renderer sits behind an interface that users can replace or choose among.

G7.name: Embeddable
G7.yes_means: The host owns the event loop and the frame; the framework is a library the host calls.
G7.why: Integrates into engines and existing apps.

H1.name: Text: shaping, bidi, IME
H1.yes_means: Complex-script shaping, bidirectional text and input-method editing all work.

H2.name: Accessibility tree
H2.yes_means: Exposes a screen-reader tree to the OS.

H3.name: Stable 1.0+ API
H3.yes_means: Has shipped a stable major version.
